correctness.summary: The threshold theorem is correct. For a block diagonal multiplier from the q-sum to the p-sum, Hölder gives the exact l_r norm of the block norms, with the c0 endpoint obtained from finite supports. The explicit threshold projection therefore gives the stated upper bound. Conversely, averaging any projection over simultaneous block sign changes preserves its norm and its range while killing off-diagonal blocks on finitely supported inputs. The resulting block coefficients satisfy A_n+lambda_n B_n=I, |lambda_n| ||A_n||<=K and ||diag(B_n)||_{X_q->X_p}<=K. Thus |lambda_n|>2K forces ||B_n||>1/(2|lambda_n|), yielding L_lambda(2K)<=2K and the lower bound Theta/2. The maximal diagonal graph is closed, and the power-weight finite-section regimes follow from elementary tail estimates: bounded for alpha<=0 or alpha>delta, N^{min(alpha,delta-alpha)} for 0<alpha<delta, and (log N)^delta at alpha=delta.

limitations: The result concerns diagonal graphs between the specified direct-sum spaces, not arbitrary closed operator graphs.
The constants 1/2 and 2^(1/p) are universal bounds rather than an exact projection constant in every case.
The 1973/1976/1978 classical papers were not read in full in this audit because no verified PDF could be retrieved.
Originality is intentionally restricted to the quantitative threshold law and its stated consequences.

literature_access.open_access_attempt: Publisher/EuDML landing pages were found; the 1976 and 1978 pages advertise free CC-BY downloads, but direct PDF retrieval returned access errors in the available web path.
literature_access.oxford_attempt: Authorized institutional retrieval returned no verified PDF for each source.

originality.summary: The 1970s Wojtaszczyk/Edelstein-Wojtaszczyk papers and the modern Albiac-Ansorena treatment are genuine classical antecedents for qualitative complemented/unconditional structure in l_p direct sums. Current targeted searches did not locate the record's quantitative reciprocal-tail formula for maximal diagonal graphs with arbitrary Banach blocks or the stated power-weight projection-constant phase diagram. However, the 1973, 1976 and 1978 Studia papers could not be inspected in full in this run. The 1976 and 1978 publisher pages advertise CC-BY downloads, but the PDF endpoints returned access errors; authorized institutional retrieval for all three returned no verified PDF. Originality is therefore accepted only for the quantitative formulation, with the unread classical papers explicitly retained as prior-art risk.

scientific_value.summary: The result gives a two-sided numerical projection-constant law and a complete complementability criterion that is independent of block dimension and internal Banach geometry. The re-entrant power-weight transition and finite-section growth rates are useful quantitative refinements of the surrounding qualitative theory.
